evidence.excerpt: In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. The framework adds a single hyperparameter controlling constraint weight and remains tractable for datasets up to 500,000 samples with an RBF kernel. Ablation studies confirm that gains diminish beyond 15% label density, at which point a supervised SVM becomes preferable.
